meta.portfolio_positioning: We recommend offering the two buildings together, with a separate price for each, and taking offers on either or both. Each ownership entity closes its own sale and identifies its own exchange property, and the buyer who wants the whole corner can buy it in one escrow. On entitlement, the city's draft Downtown TOD Specific Plan would allow about 72 units across the corner at 87 units per acre, against 37 today, but it is not adopted, and a redevelopment would carry relocation obligations on every occupied unit. We would not recommend entitling before a sale; the buyer who wants that upside pays for the corner and carries the timeline.

overview: The LAAA Team of Marcus & Millichap is pleased to present 905 N 3rd Street, a 31-unit apartment building in Downtown Burbank. The two-story wood frame building was built in 1972 and holds 27 one bedroom and 4 two bedroom units, 20,281 square feet on a 26,397 square foot lot. Tenants share a pool and a fitness room. The building is covered by AB 1482 and Burbank's Tenant Protection Ordinance.
The investment case is a fully occupied building with its roof work done. Scheduled rent sits about 8.6% under market, and a new TPO roof was permitted on the main building in November 2024.

location_narrative: The property sits at N 3rd Street and E Burbank Boulevard on the northwest edge of Downtown Burbank. Burbank Town Center is 0.35 miles southeast and McCambridge Park 0.5 miles northwest, and Walk Score rates the block 91 for its access to daily errands.

The Downtown Burbank Metrolink station is 0.8 miles southeast, and the NoHo to Pasadena bus rapid transit line stops on Olive Avenue about 0.6 miles away. Hollywood Burbank Airport is 2.0 miles west. Walt Disney Studios is 2.2 miles south, Providence Saint Joseph Medical Center 2.3 miles south and Warner Bros. Studios 2.9 miles southwest.

ZIP 91502 is 90% renter-occupied, with a median household income of $52,473 and a median gross rent of $1,916. The city's draft Downtown TOD Specific Plan, dated 06/23/2026, would raise this block to 87 units per acre, with hearings targeted for late fall 2026.
physical_narrative: The building is wood frame, built in 1972, 20,281 SF per the county on a 26,397 SF lot, with a pool. City building records show a new TPO membrane on 11,400 SF of the main building's flat roof permitted in November 2024, a shingle re-roof in 2017, a full tear-off re-roof in 2003, sewer line replacements on both sides of the building in 2016 and under unit 101 in 2019, and an entry enclosure creating the lobby and office in 2002.
The rent roll does not carry unit sizes that add up to the county's building area, so unit sizes here are estimates: about 575 SF for a one bedroom and 800 SF for a two bedroom.

Burbank's soft-story ordinance applies to wood frame buildings designed before 1978 with open or weak ground floors, with engineered plans due 01/11/2027. A buyer will ask whether the building is in scope and where it stands, so that answer belongs in the offering before it goes out.
market_narrative: Six Burbank apartment sales of 11 to 24 units closed between December 2025 and September 2026 at $264,643 to $380,769 per unit and 10.56 to 13.44 times gross rent. The closest in age and size, 1799 N Hollywood Way, 13 units built in 1963, closed at $3.45M in December 2025, $265,385 per unit, a 6.26% cap on its own income. 233-237 N Hollywood Way, 14 units, closed at $3.705M, a 5.95% cap, and 615 E Magnolia Boulevard, 11 units, at $3.0M, a 6.66% cap.
Thirty days before each of those sales closed, the 5-year Treasury ran 3.6% to 4.4%. On 09/18/2026 it stood at 4.86% (Federal Reserve Bank of St. Louis, FRED series DGS5).
A buyer today pays more for money than the buyers who set those comps. That is why the recommended price sits at a 6.0% cap, at the middle of the comparable yields rather than the low end of them.
positioning_narrative: The right buyer wants a fully occupied 31-unit building with a new roof, rents 8.6% under market and a Downtown Burbank corner that the city is planning for more density. That buyer should be qualified early on how they will handle the soft-story question and the building's financing, because those decide whether an offer holds through escrow.
rent_narrative: One bedrooms in the thirteen closest comparable Burbank buildings, built 1961 to 1977 within about a mile and a quarter, run $1,699 to $2,325 with a median of $2,000; a one bedroom at 600 E Harvard Road came off the market at $2,075 after 31 days. Two bedrooms run a median of $2,550 across the seven closest matches, and one at 600 E Harvard Road came off the market at $2,575 after ten days.
Market rent is $2,075 for a one bedroom and $2,575 for a two bedroom, above the building's highest in-place rents of $2,054 and $2,525. The pro forma carries every unit at those rents.
valuation_narrative: The recommended list price is $7,550,000, $243,548 per unit and $372 per SF, with an opinion of value of $7,350,000 to $7,650,000. Current scheduled rent of $733,136 less a 3% vacancy reserve gives $711,142 of effective gross income. Operating expenses of $258,724, with taxes reassessed at the list price, leave net operating income of $452,418: a 5.99% cap rate and a 10.30 gross rent multiplier. At market rents the net operating income is $510,864, a 6.77% cap rate.

The price sits at a 6.0% cap, near the middle of the comparable yields, while the gross rent multiplier and the price per unit sit below every sale in the set. Those comps priced on cheaper money, so a buyer at today's rates can pay this price and still reach a positive return.
